evidence: NESTING (static, verified): task/task.toml:18 [agent].timeout_sec=7200.0, :21 build_timeout_sec=600.0, :27 [verifier].timeout_sec=13200.0. task/tests/test.sh:207 runs each suite as `timeout "$budget_sec" rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1 ...` so judges in a suite run sequentially; :213 gates budget 1500, :224 scored budget 11100. Judge timeouts (judge.toml line 4 each): gates/render 600 + gates/constraints 600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack); scored/functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s slack); each single judge < its suite budget; gates+scored budgets 1500+11100 = 12600 < 13200 (600 s slack for setup, cp -a /app, liveness, prompt substitution, two score.py runs); sum of all judges 12000 < 13200 (internal annotation satisfied). Liveness: test.sh:115-122 polls up to 120 x (0.25 s sleep + probe with 2 s urlopen timeout per URL) - ~30 s for an app that refuses connections until ready, worst case ~510 s for an accept-but-hang app, still inside the 600 s verifier slack when suites themselves do not time out. Restart helper (test.sh:155-177) ~5 s kill wait + ~30 s readiness < restart_mcp.py:11 HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC=55. All of task.toml timeouts, test.sh (diff: identical), tests/Dockerfile (identical), restart_mcp.py (identical) and all five judge.toml [judge] headers (identical) match the frozen template, so budgets are canonical and unchanged, consistent with REVIEW_POLICY 'current budgets remain unchanged'. Build: environment/Dockerfile only apt-installs 4 packages and `npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1` on node:22-bookworm-slim (prebuilt binaries) - 600 s is ample for a realistic cold build on public network (not timed by me). WORKLOAD (unmeasured, the row's 'long enough' half): the functional dimension has 43 [[criterion]] blocks in one batched claude-code/GLM-5.3-flashx judge capped at 9000 s, driven by a 15.9 KB protocol (prompt.md:25-51, protocols Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D) with 9 'independent context' set-ups, 17 request-replay instructions, ~14 sub-steps in protocol B alone, many account switches (Rafael, Mei, Ingrid, Bill, Aud, Tomas, Noor, Lena, anonymous), several 'wait up to 15 seconds' live readings in U and V, Activity reconciliation and a final restart. raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; every entry is 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'. No target-builder run measures whether 7200 s fits the agent build either. Per SKILL ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass') and REVIEW_POLICY ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number'; 'Scripted Playwright duration is not LLM judge duration'), the nesting half passes but 'long enough' cannot be credited, so the row is Not exercised with risk. I am not filing a Fail because the overrun is an inference, not a measurement, and the budgets are the canonical template values.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that could be graded wrongly: a fully correct app whose board renders more DOM per card (richer accessible snapshots) or whose live updates arrive near the 15 s windows makes the single functional judge consume more turns/tokens; if the batched functional judge exceeds 9000 s (or the scored suite exceeds 11100 s), test.sh:224-226 `if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0; fi` leaves the plain zero reward from write_zero_reward, so a correct submission that passed both gates receives 0.0 for a harness-capacity reason, not an app defect. Broken app check: an app that accepts TCP but never answers costs up to ~510 s of liveness polling, still within the 600 s verifier slack, and fails the gates anyway, so no weak app passes because of timeouts. Neither scenario is measured.
suggested_fix: Do not change budgets automatically: run at least one full configured verifier (gates + scored, claude-code with z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx) on the frozen golden, record per-judge wall time from rewardkit logs and record it as hash-bound workload evidence; if functional approaches 9000 s, reduce protocol scope/redundant browser work together with the public scope, or seek explicit lead authorization for a justified sub-five-hour timeout change with the measured reason.
